and it will mix itself with the liquids of its own fountain. Therefore, there are gods who are the leaders of all species. These are followed by gods whose leader is <term>ousia</term> <gloss>essence or substance</gloss>. These are the sensible gods, alike in their dual origin <note>referring to their nature being both divine and material</note>, who produce all things through sensible nature. Each one illuminates his own work, one through another. The leader of the essence <note>original: "ousiarches"</note> of heaven, or whatever is understood by that name, is Jupiter. For through heaven, Jupiter provides life to all. The leader of the essence of the sun is Light. For the goodness of light is infused into us through the orb of the sun. There are thirty-six <note>referring to the Decans of the zodiac</note> who are called <term>Horoskopoi</term> <gloss>Horoscopes or Hour-watchers</gloss>. These are the stars always fixed in the same place. Their leader of essence or prince is he whom they call <term>Pantomorphos</term> <gloss>All-formed or Omniform</gloss>, who creates different forms from diverse species. The seven spheres which are called "wandering" <note>the planets</note> have their own <term>ousiarchas</term> <gloss>leaders of essence</gloss>, that is, their own princes, whom they call Fortune or <term>Heimarmene</term> <gloss>Fate</gloss>. By these, all things are changed by the law of nature with the firmest stability, varied by eternal movement. The air, truly, is the instrument or the engine of all, through which all things are made. Moreover, the leader of essence of this <note>the air</note> is the second <note>likely referring to a secondary demiurgic power</note>. He gives mortal things to mortals and things similar to these. These things being so, moving from the lowest to the highest, all things are thus connected to one another according to their nature, so that mortal things are linked to mortals and sensible things to sensibles. The highest power of governance obeys that highest Lord, so that they are not many, but rather one. For since all things hang from the One, and rather flow down from Him, when they are seen at a distance, they are believed to be many and divided. Yet, united, they are one, or rather two: that from which all things are made, and he by whom they are made. That is, from the matter of which they are made, and from his will, by whose nod the others are produced. ASCLEPIUS: What is this reasoning again, O Trismegistus? TRISMEGISTUS: It is this, O Asclepius. God, indeed, is either the Father or the Lord.

<margin>GENTILIA <note>Refers to the "Nations" or "Gentiles," likely categorizing the types of deities discussed.</note></margin>
<margin>Jupiter.</margin>
<margin>Light.</margin>
<margin>Horoscopes.</margin>
<margin>Pantomorphos.</margin>

<summary>Hermes explains the hierarchy of divine governors, including Jupiter as the ruler of heaven and the thirty-six Decans, concluding that all diverse celestial influences originate from a single divine source and will.</summary>
<keywords>Jupiter, Ousia, Ousiarches, Sun, Light, Horoscopes, Decans, Pantomorphos, Planets, Fate, Heimarmene, Unity of God</keywords>
